case_name: Charles W. Monroe and Rebecca A. Monroe v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Family size of two; fully stipulated case under Rule 122.

adjustments: PTC disallowed because household income exceeded 400% of federal poverty line (excess APTC)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Eligibility for premium tax credit (effect of §86(e) election on MAGI)
conceded: Petitioners allowed additional State and local tax deduction of $87
Petitioners allowed additional withholding credit of $269
Petitioners failed to report wages of $5,207
Petitioners failed to report unemployment benefits of $237
Petitioners liable for 6662(a) penalty attributable to unreported wages and unemployment benefits; not liable for penalty attributable to other items

findings_of_fact.fact: Husband received $35,651.80 Social Security benefits in 2015
findings_of_fact.snippet: In 2015 petitioner husband received $35,651.80 of Social Security benefits.

findings_of_fact.fact: Payment components: $5,297 2015 benefits; lump sums $348 (2014), $10,247 (2013), $10,943 (2012), $2,607 (2011); $6,000 attorney fees; $209.80 Medicare Part B premiums
findings_of_fact.snippet: $10,247 lump-sum payment related to 2013; (4) a $10,943 lump-sum payment related to 2012; (5) a $2,607 lump-sum payment related to 2011

findings_of_fact.fact: Enrolled in California marketplace plan Jan 1-Aug 31, 2015; APTC $1,059/month, total $8,472
Joint return with §86(e) election; AGI $38,497 = wages $34,176 + unemployment $237 + taxable SS $4,084
findings_of_fact.snippet: they had adjusted gross income of $38,497, consisting of $34,176 of wages, $237 of unemployment compensation, and $4,084 of taxable Social Security benefits
They have a family size oftwo people for Federal income tax purposes.

findings_of_fact.fact: Stipulated: under respondent's view MAGI is $70,065.80, which exceeds 400% FPL; under petitioners' view MAGI is below 400% FPL
findings_of_fact.snippet: the parties have stipulated that $70,065.80 exceeds 400% of the amount equal to the Federal poverty line

findings_of_fact.fact: Footnote: MAGI consists of $35,652.80 SS benefits, $34,176 wages, $237 unemployment
findings_of_fact.snippet: This consists of $35,652.80 of Social Security benefits, $34,176 of wages, and $237 ofunemployment compensation.

issues.question: Premium tax credit (§36B): does MAGI include all Social Security benefits received in 2015 notwithstanding a §86(e) lump-sum election, making household income exceed 400% of FPL?
issues.holding: Following Johnson v. Commissioner, 152 T.C. (2019), MAGI includes all SS benefits received regardless of §86(e) election; MAGI exceeds 400% FPL; petitioners ineligible for PTC
issues.computable_reason: Pure statutory construction on stipulated numbers; MAGI vs 400% FPL threshold comparison

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Petitioners ineligible for 2015 PTC; concessions reflected in Rule 155 computation; 6662 penalty only as to unreported wages/unemployment (conceded)

notes: Discrepancy in opinion: SS benefits stated as $35,651.80 (p. 2) and $35,652.80 (fn. 6); $70,065.80 = 35,652.80 + 34,176 + 237 (derived). FPL dollar amount not stated (exceedance stipulated). After NOD respondent issued updated report reducing taxable SS per §86(e) election. Fully stipulated (Rule 122).
